## Direct Instruction: The Gift of the Nile 尼罗河的礼物

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
- **The Longest River (世界最长河流):** Flows **NORTH** over 4,100 miles from the East African highlands into the Mediterranean Sea.
- **A Predictable Flood (可预测的泛滥):** Every **July** the Nile rose; by **October** it receded, leaving a rich layer of black **{{< vocab "silt" >}}** (*Kemet* / 黑土).
- **Two Regions (上下埃及):**
  - **Upper Egypt (上埃及):** High-elevation narrow southern valley down to the First **{{< vocab "cataract" text="Cataract" >}}** (瀑布/急流).
  - **Lower Egypt (下埃及):** Broad, marshy northern **{{< vocab "delta" >}}** (三角洲) at the Mediterranean mouth.
- **Deserts as Walls (沙漠屏障):** Sahara and Eastern deserts blocked invasions and spared Egypt the constant warfare of the {{< vocab "Fertile Crescent" >}}.
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
![](images/nile-satellite-view.png){fig-alt="NASA Landsat satellite view of the Nile River" height="320px"}

::: {.small-note}
Greek historian **Herodotus**: Egypt was *"the gift of the Nile."*
:::
:::
::::

## The Nile: A Gift with Conditions 有条件的礼物

| Environmental Condition 环境挑战 | Egyptian Solution 古埃及人的应对方案 |
|---|---|
| **Flood too HIGH (洪水过高)**<br>Destroys mud-brick homes, granaries, and canals | **Built dikes, reservoirs & {{< vocab "irrigation" >}} ditches**<br>修筑防洪堤坝、水库与灌溉水渠 |
| **Flood too LOW (洪水过低)**<br>Leaves no {{< vocab "silt" >}} or water → crop failure and famine | **Stored grain {{< vocab "surplus" >}} in royal granaries**<br>丰年由国家粮仓储备余粮以备荒年 |
| **Travel & Defense along the River**<br>Churning rapids at the First {{< vocab "cataract" text="Cataract" >}}; vast deserts on both sides | **Used north-flowing current & south-blowing winds**<br>顺流向北航行，扬帆借北风向南逆流而上 |

::: {.callout-tip title="Think · 思考" icon=false}
Why was a **predictable** flood so much better for farmers than the violent, unpredictable floods of the Tigris and Euphrates?
:::

## Direct Instruction: Egypt Unites into a Kingdom 埃及统一为王国

::: {.timeline}
- **c. 5000 B.C. · Farming Villages Along the Nile (农业村落)**
  Each village had its own rituals, gods, and chieftain.
- **c. 3200 B.C. · Two Separate Kingdoms (上下埃及两个王国)**
  **Upper Egypt** (south, tall **White Crown**) and **Lower Egypt** (north delta, **Red Crown**).
- **c. 3000 B.C. · King Narmer Unites Egypt (纳尔迈统一上下埃及)**
  The carved **Narmer Palette** shows **King Narmer** wearing the **Double Crown** (红白双冠 — two lands, one ruler). He founded his capital at **Memphis (孟菲斯)** where Upper and Lower Egypt met, launching **31 {{< vocab "dynasty" text="dynasties" >}}** over 2,600 years.
- **2660–2180 B.C. · The Old Kingdom (古王国时期)**
  The great age of {{< vocab "pharaoh" text="pharaohs" >}}, **{{< vocab "theocracy" >}}**, and **{{< vocab "pyramid" >}}** building.
:::

## Direct Instruction: Pharaohs Rule as Gods 法老以神之名统治

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **{{< vocab "theocracy" text="Theocracy" >}} (神权政治):** Government in which rule is based on religious authority — the {{< vocab "pharaoh" >}} was both the political and religious leader.
- Unlike Mesopotamian kings (seen as *servants/representatives* of the gods), Egyptian **{{< vocab "pharaoh" text="pharaohs" >}} were living gods**.
- Egyptians believed the pharaoh caused:
  1. **The sun to rise** every morning;
  2. **The Nile to flood** every July;
  3. **The crops to grow** and truth/justice (*ma'at*) to prevail.
- **The Eternal {{< vocab "ka" text="Ka" >}} (永恒的“卡”):** Because a king's spirit (**{{< vocab "ka" >}}**) continued to govern Egypt after death, his eternal tomb ({{< vocab "pyramid" >}}) was even more important than his palace!
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note title="Major Egyptian Deities · 主要神祇" icon=false}
- **Re (拉):** Sun god; the most important deity.
- **Osiris (奥西里斯):** God of the dead and ruler of the underworld.
- **Isis (伊西斯):** Goddess representing the ideal mother and wife.
- **Anubis (阿努比斯):** Jackal-headed god and guide of the underworld who weighed dead souls' hearts.
:::
:::
::::

## Builders of the Great Pyramid 金字塔的建造者

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](images/great-pyramid-giza.png){fig-alt="Great Pyramid of Giza cutaway diagram"}
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- **By the Numbers (吉萨大金字塔数据):**
  - **481 feet tall** (taller than a 40-story building), covering **13 acres**
  - **2,000,000+ limestone & granite blocks**, weighing **2.5 to 15 tons** each
  - Built **without the wheel** and **without iron tools**!
- **Who Built Them? (建造者是谁？)**
  - **Peasant labourers** (not slaves!) working for the state during the July–October flood season when fields were underwater, provided with food and housing.
  - Work crews carved their proud team nicknames inside the stones: *"The Vigorous Gang"* (活力队), *"The Enduring Gang"* (耐久队), *"The Craftsman Gang"* (工匠队).
:::
::::

## Direct Instruction: Mummification & Herodotus 木乃伊制作与希罗多德

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
![](images/herodotus-bust.png){fig-alt="Marble bust of Herodotus" height="270px"}

::: {.small-note}
**Herodotus** (c. 484–425 B.C.), Greek historian who recorded Egyptian embalming in *The Histories*, Book II.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
**Why {{< vocab "mummification" >}}?** To preserve the body so the **{{< vocab "ka" >}}** could recognize and return to it in the afterlife.

**Herodotus's 7 Steps (Sequence in FA5):**
1. **Remove the brain** through the nostrils with an iron hook.
2. **Make an incision** in the side and **remove the internal organs** (placed in four **Canopic Jars** guarded by the Sons of Horus; the **heart was left inside** for judgment!).
3. **Fill the belly** with pure myrrh, cassia, and perfumes.
4. **Sew up** the belly.
5. **Steep in natron** (natural drying mineral salt) for **70 days**.
6. **Wash the corpse** after 70 days.
7. **Wrap the whole body** in waxen linen bandages and place in the tomb with the ***Book of the Dead* (《亡灵书》)**.
:::
::::

# Period 3: Writing, Science & the Rise and Fall of Power 第3节：文字、科技与兴衰 {background-color="#003477"}

**Big Question · 核心问题:** What made Egypt's {{< vocab "civilization" >}} last 3,000 years — and how do we still read it today? *(是什么让古埃及文明延续 3000 年？我们今天又如何读懂它？)*

## Direct Instruction: Hieroglyphics, Papyrus & the Rosetta Stone

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](images/rosetta-stone.png){fig-alt="The Rosetta Stone at the British Museum" height="360px"}
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
- **{{< vocab "hieroglyphics" text="Hieroglyphics" >}} (象形文字):** Greek for *"sacred carving."* Pictures first stood for objects/ideas, and later for **sounds** (like an owl for the *m* sound).
- **{{< vocab "papyrus" text="Papyrus" >}} (纸莎草纸):** Split reeds from the marshy Nile {{< vocab "delta" >}}, pressed crosswise into lightweight paper-like scrolls — much easier to carry and store than Mesopotamian clay tablets!
- **The {{< vocab "Rosetta Stone" >}} (罗塞塔石碑):**
  - Found in **1799** by French soldiers near Rosetta in the Nile Delta.
  - Carved in **196 B.C.** with the **same royal decree in three scripts**: (1) **{{< vocab "hieroglyphics" >}}**, (2) **Demotic** (everyday Egyptian script), and (3) **Ancient Greek**.
  - Because scholars already knew **Ancient Greek**, French scholar **Jean-François Champollion** unlocked hieroglyphics in **1822**!
:::
::::

## Direct Instruction: Practical Science & Technology 实用科学与技术

| Egyptian Innovation 埃及科技成就 | Practical Problem Solved 解决的实际问题 |
|---|---|
| **365-Day Solar Calendar (365天太阳历)** | Priests tracked the star **Sirius (天狼星)** appearing right before the July flood → **12 months of 30 days + 5 holiday days** (accurate to within 6 hours of the true solar year!). |
| **Written Numbers & Geometry (算术与几何)** | Used to **re-survey farm boundaries** washed away by the annual Nile flood, calculate grain taxes, and engineer precise {{< vocab "pyramid" text="pyramids" >}} and stone columns. |
| **Medicine & Surgery (医学与外科)** | Doctors checked **heart rate by feeling the pulse**, set broken bones with **splints**, treated wounds and fevers, and performed surgery. |

## Direct Instruction: Life in Egyptian Society 埃及社会金字塔

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](images/egyptian-social-pyramid.png){fig-alt="Egyptian Social Pyramid diagram" height="360px"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
1. **Top (顶层):** **King ({{< vocab "pharaoh" text="Pharaoh" >}}), Queen & Royal Family**
2. **Upper Class (上层阶级):** Wealthy landowners, government officials, priests, and army commanders.
3. **Middle Class (中层阶级):** Merchants and skilled artisans.
4. **Lower Class (底层阶级 — Largest Group):** Peasant farmers and laborers (plus enslaved war captives in later periods).

::: {.callout-tip title="Social Mobility & Women's Rights · 阶层流动与女性权利" icon=false}
- **Literacy = Mobility:** Anyone who learned to read and write {{< vocab "hieroglyphics" >}} could rise to high office in the army, treasury, priesthood, or royal court.
- **Egyptian Women:** Could **own and trade property**, **propose marriage**, and **seek divorce** (keeping **one-third** of the couple's property!).
:::
:::
::::

## The Rise and Fall of Power & Comparison with Mesopotamia

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Timeline of Egyptian Power:**
- **Old Kingdom (c. 2660–2180 B.C.):** Great age of pyramid building; collapsed when pharaohs' power declined.
- **Middle Kingdom (c. 2040–1640 B.C.):** Order restored; dug **Nile–Red Sea canal**, built dikes, drained delta swamps for new farmland.
- **Hyksos Invasion (1640–1523 B.C.):** West Asian **Hyksos** (*"rulers of foreign lands"*) crossed Suez on horse-drawn chariots and ruled Egypt for a century — before Egypt rose again in the **New Kingdom**.
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
| Dimension 维度 | Ancient Egypt 古埃及 | {{< vocab "Mesopotamia" >}} 两河流域 |
|---|---|---|
| **Rivers** | One river: **Nile** (flows north) | Two rivers: **Tigris & Euphrates** |
| **Floods** | **Predictable** every July | **Unpredictable**, violent floods |
| **Barriers** | **Deserts, seas & {{< vocab "cataract" text="cataracts" >}}** | **Flat open plain** (no barriers) |
| **Government** | Unified **{{< vocab "theocracy" >}}** ({{< vocab "pharaoh" >}} = god) | Competing **{{< vocab "city-state" text="city-states" >}}** → shifting empires |
| **Afterlife** | Optimistic **Other World** ({{< vocab "ka" >}}) | Gloomy *"land of no return"* |
| **Writing** | **{{< vocab "hieroglyphics" text="Hieroglyphics" >}}** on **{{< vocab "papyrus" >}}** | **{{< vocab "cuneiform" text="Cuneiform" >}}** on clay tablets |
:::
::::
